seoTitle: How to Add a Header and Footer in Google Sheets
metaDescription: Add headers and footers to a Google Sheets printout, including page numbers and custom text, using the built-in print settings panel.
intro: Preparing a spreadsheet for printing or PDF export often means adding headers and footers with page numbers, titles, or dates so the document looks organized. Google Sheets has a dedicated print layout panel for this, and this guide walks through enabling and customizing those fields.

steps.heading: Open the print settings menu
steps.body: Go to File and open the print settings panel for your spreadsheet.

steps.heading: Find the Headers and Footers section
steps.body: Locate the sidebar section dedicated to headers and footers within the print layout.

steps.heading: Enable default attributes
steps.body: Turn on checkboxes for default fields like sheet name and current date.

steps.heading: Open Edit Custom Fields
steps.body: Use the custom fields wizard to type in personalized text entries for your header or footer.

steps.heading: Position your text and page numbers
steps.body: Place page numbers, titles, and timestamps in the left, center, or right boxes as needed.

steps.heading: Confirm and preview
steps.body: Save your changes and preview the final layout to confirm it looks right before exporting or printing.

faq.question: Can I add page numbers automatically?
faq.answer: Yes, default attribute checkboxes let you enable page numbers along with other fields like the current date.

faq.question: Can I repeat frozen rows across multiple printed pages?
faq.answer: Yes, the print layout panel includes an option to repeat frozen row titles automatically on every printed page.

faq.question: Where do custom header text entries go?
faq.answer: The Edit Custom Fields wizard lets you type personalized text and position it in the left, center, or right sections of the header or footer.

faq.question: Do header and footer settings affect the on-screen spreadsheet view?
faq.answer: No, these settings only apply to the printed or exported PDF version, not your regular editing view.
